headline: High: Dify can write and egress broadly, but the paired awesome-list has no runtime surfaces, so interaction risks are mostly one-way and limited to documentation-driven misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default channel exists for prompt injection: agent_a is an un-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b’s documented file and tool surfaces do not connect to agent_a. Without a shared channel, agent_a cannot inject instructions into agent_b.
conditions: IF agent_a is manually copied into agent_b as prompt text, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added between them, reassess for instruction smuggling.
mitigations: Keep agent_a as a static reference list, not prompt input.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into agent_b system prompts.
Require provenance labels on any imported content.
Add a review step before agent_b executes instructions from files.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking for shared inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no runtime I/O, while agent_b reads uploaded knowledge-base files and conversation logs. The pair does not show a shared workspace or direct data flow, so leakage is limited unless operator copies sensitive content into agent_b or stores it in shared files.
conditions: IF sensitive files are uploaded into agent_b’s knowledge base, they may be retained in conversation logs.
IF agent_a is used as a source document and copied into agent_b, any embedded secrets can flow into outputs.
mitigations: Avoid uploading secrets to agent_b knowledge bases.
Redact sensitive text before copying between systems.
Restrict conversation-log retention in agent_b.
Use separate storage locations for reference material and operational data.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploaded knowledge-base files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write, shell, or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. agent_b can write files and spawn subprocesses, but there is no second writer or shared mutable target documented, so no capability conflict pathway is established.
conditions: IF agent_a is replaced with a runnable agent that writes to the same directory as agent_b, conflict risk appears.
IF multiple agent_b instances share a writable workspace without locking, write conflicts may occur.
mitigations: Keep agent_a non-runnable.
Assign agent_b a dedicated workspace per conversation.
Avoid shared git or filesystem targets across instances.
Use file locks for any shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a curated list, not an action-taking agent, so it cannot generate operational facts for agent_b by default. agent_b can act on tool outputs, but there is no documented pipeline where agent_a’s output becomes authoritative input to agent_b, making cascading error possible only through manual reuse.
conditions: IF operator copies claims from agent_a into agent_b prompts without verification, downstream errors can cascade.
IF agent_b is configured to trust imported text as facts, false guidance can propagate.
mitigations: Treat agent_a as a directory, not a source of truth.
Verify any copied guidance against primary docs before execution.
Require citations for operational claims in agent_b prompts.
Add a human review step before agent_b acts on imported content.
requires-engineering: implement fact-checking or citation validation in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b handles conversation logs and knowledge-base files, which can create retention or residency issues if regulated data is uploaded. agent_a has no data classes touched and no runtime, so it is not the compliance driver here. The pair shows a possible policy mismatch only through agent_b’s storage behavior.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into agent_b, its conversation-log retention policy must match the data class.
IF the deployment stores knowledge-base files in a restricted jurisdiction, residency controls must be verified.
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data unless retention is approved.
Review agent_b log-retention settings before use.
Separate public knowledge bases from regulated datasets.
Document data residency for uploaded files.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
